review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes at all. I looked at its evaluation lemmas (germ_X, germ_scalar, projectiveChartRingHom_mk/_ratio/_constants, homogeneousFieldEval_mk) and checked how they are used, in this file and with grep in sibling files. I did not recommend simp for general identities. The findings cover only lemmas that are applied by hand again and again, either with rw or by listing them in `simp only`/`simp`, and whose left-hand sides are evaluation forms that rewrite toward simpler terms. I could not run Lean, so I did not check simp-set interactions (for example with Mathlib's MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom simp lemmas) or termination. I also did not check whether the explicit proof arguments in the `mk` lemmas unify cleanly as simp patterns. Those points are untested. The germ_scalar point is weaker and depends on how its uses change.

findings.problem: This is the canonical evaluation of the chart coordinate. Its left side is a germ applied to the image of X, and its right side is the plain function-field element `a`, so it only simplifies terms. It carries no simp attribute, so every use has to name it by hand: `simpa only [B.germ_X]` (line 118), `simp [x,y,map_pow,B.germ_X]` (line 184) and `simp only [...,A.germ_X]` (line 186). In `compatible` goals, `map_pow` turns `B.germ ((B.poly X)^d)` into `(B.germ (B.poly X))^d`. Without simp the reader must remember to add germ_X each time. RelativeAmpleness.lean (line 114) also applies it manually.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`: `@[simp] lemma PolynomialCurveChart.germ_X ...`. The left side has head `PolynomialCurveChart.germ` and the right side is a variable, so there is no cycle. Then drop `B.germ_X`/`A.germ_X` from the explicit simp lists at lines 118, 184 and 186. Add a matching `@[simp]` pointwise lemma for `germ_scalar`, for example `A.germ (A.scalar c) = curveFieldScalar sC c`. The existing statement is a `RingHom.comp` equation, which simp cannot use on applied terms and which the proof at line 107 only reaches after `change`.
findings.benefit: Chart-coordinate computations can be closed by plain `simp`. Each proof no longer needs a hand-written list of chart lemmas.

findings.excerpt: lemma projectiveChartRingHom_mk (c : k →+* R) (x : σ → R)
findings.problem: This is the defining evaluation rule for `projectiveChartRingHom` on `Away.mk`. It, `projectiveChartRingHom_ratio` and `projectiveChartRingHom_constants` carry no simp attribute. Every consumer rewrites by hand: `rw [projectiveChartRingHom_mk, map_pow, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X', pow_one]` (line 312), `rw [projectiveChartRingHom_mk]` in `_ratio` (line 238), `simp only [..., projectiveChartRingHom_mk, ...]` (line 492), and an explicit `.trans` in `_constants` (line 245). SurfaceSquare.lean line 57, CompleteIntersections.lean line 406 and ProjectiveCoordinates.lean line 572 repeat the same `rw [projectiveChartRingHom_mk,map_pow,pow_one]` pattern. The `_ratio` and `_constants` lemmas also have to be passed to `simp only` by name (lines 255–258).
findings.proposed_change: Mark `projectiveChartRingHom_mk` `@[simp]`. Its right side `MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom c x p` is strictly simpler, and the left side has a distinct head symbol, `projectiveChartRingHom` applied to `Away.mk`. Also mark `projectiveChartRingHom_ratio` and `projectiveChartRingHom_constants` `@[simp]`, since they give the canonical values `x j` and `c a`. Make sure the `_ratio` pattern, which uses `projectiveChartRatio`, does not clash with the `mk` rule. The `mk` rule could be given higher priority, or `projectiveChartRatio` could be kept irreducible to simp. Then the chains at lines 312 and 492 and the SurfaceSquare, CompleteIntersections and ProjectiveCoordinates sites can be `simp`.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical way to evaluate the chart ring map. Downstream proofs about projective charts shrink to `simp`, and nobody has to remember the lemma name at each site.

findings.excerpt: homogeneousFieldEval 𝒜 h f hf (Away.mk 𝒜 hfd n a ha) = h a * (h f)⁻¹ ^ n
findings.problem: This is the only evaluation rule for `homogeneousFieldEval` on generators. It is not a simp lemma, although its right side is a closed form in the target field. Both later proofs apply it by hand with the repeated rewrite `rw [homogeneousFieldEval_mk, homogeneousFieldEval_mk]`, in `homogeneousFieldEval_awayMap` (line 378) and `projectiveFieldMap_scaling` (line 461). Each time it is followed by manual `simp only [map_mul, map_pow, mul_inv_rev, mul_pow]` and a `calc`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `homogeneousFieldEval_mk` `@[simp]`, since the left side is headed by `homogeneousFieldEval` applied to `Away.mk`. Replace the double `rw` with `simp only [homogeneousFieldEval_mk, ...]` or plain `simp`. Check the `awayMap_mk` interaction before relying on a bare `simp`. If a global attribute is too aggressive, at least use `simp only [homogeneousFieldEval_mk]` in place of the doubled `rw`.
findings.benefit: Each `homogeneousFieldEval` computation is handled by the simp set instead of by counting how many `rw` steps are needed. The `calc` blocks are left with only the field arithmetic.
